content: 1. The use of high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 2. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates and associated with serious or life-threatening events at elevated plasma concentrations should be used cautiously with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 4. Co-administration of cidofovir with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Combining emtricitabine and tenofovir with other drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, such as cidofovir, increases the risk of nephrotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are required. 6. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is necessary. 7. Cobicistat inhibits CYP2D6, and caution is required when using CYP2D6 substrates with elevated plasma concentrations that may lead to serious or life-threatening events. 8. Cisplatin and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is essential. 9. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Clarithromycin levels may increase when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce clarithromycin dosage by 50% if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 60 mL/min. 11. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted, and close monitoring is required. 12. Clonazepam levels are elevated when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing benzodiazepine doses. 13. Cobicistat inhibits P-glycoprotein (P-gp), which may increase the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cocaine topical levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Codeine levels are elevated when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Caution is advised, and therapy should be monitored closely. 16. Colchicine levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, and adjust colchicine dosage as needed. 17. Colistin and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Conivaptan levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Contrast media (iodinated) and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Crizotinib levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 21. Crofelemer may increase elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cyclophosphamide levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Cyclosporine and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Dabigatran levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to P-gp inhibition. Avoid co-administration if CrCl is less than 30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or less than 50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 25. Dabrafinib decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Danazol increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Dantrolene levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Dapsone levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition but decreased due to CYP2C9/10 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Darifenacin levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Darunavir increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Dasatinib levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 32. Deflazacort levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce deflazacort dosage to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Desipramine levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Dexamethasone levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Diazepam levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing benzodiazepine doses. 36. Diclofenac levels are decreased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP2C9/10 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Digoxin levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to P-gp inhibition. Initiate digoxin at a low dose and titrate carefully. 38. Diltiazem levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Disopyramide levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Docetaxel levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 41. Doxepin levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP2D6 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Doxorubicin levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Dronabinol levels are increased by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Dronedarone levels are elevated by elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
